official_sources.finding: Network grid access was introduced in PROJ 7.0 and can transparently fetch required grid portions when authorized.
PROJ network use requires network capability plus explicit authorization such as PROJ_NETWORK=ON, proj.ini network=on, or the context API.
The default remote grid endpoint is the PROJ CDN and can be overridden with PROJ_NETWORK_ENDPOINT or the context API.
Remote grid chunks are cached in a SQLite cache.db in the user-writable PROJ directory.
The current network documentation states that the local grid cache is enabled by default.
The current network documentation states a default cache maximum size of 300 MB.
PROJ exposes APIs to test whether a whole grid download is needed and to download a whole grid.
projsync is the official utility for pre-downloading transformation resource files instead of relying on on-demand access.
PROJ searches explicit relative or absolute resource-file paths before general search directories.
A proj_context_set_file_finder callback can override normal resource lookup.
proj_context_set_search_paths can define explicit resource search paths and override later search mechanisms.
The PROJ user-writable directory is part of resource lookup and is platform dependent.
PROJ_DATA defines resource search paths; the older PROJ_LIB name remains a fallback for compatibility in newer PROJ.
PROJ can discover ../share/proj relative to binaries or libraries when the installation layout is respected.
PROJ also has a build-time resource installation path, so a relocated installation can change lookup unless provenance is pinned.
When network is enabled, missing local grids may be resolved from remote CDN resources, so offline and online runs can select different available operations.
The proj-data package is the maintained collection of freely available PROJ resource files.
Legacy proj-datumgrid packages are not maintained for modern PROJ 7+ workflows and are retained mainly for older versions.
projsync can download resources into the user-writable directory, system directory, or an explicit target directory.
projsync can use a local files.geojson catalogue, allowing the catalogue itself to be pinned for reproducible resource selection.
projsync filters downloads using PROJ_DATA.VERSION compatibility metadata by default.
projsync --no-version-filtering disables its normal resource-version compatibility filtering and therefore changes the candidate resource set.
projsync --file can request a specific resource file by name.
projsync combines --file, --source-id, --area-of-use and --bbox filters with AND logic.
projinfo --grid-check=sort keeps missing-grid operations but sorts them lower when networking is not enabled.
projinfo --grid-check=discard_missing removes coordinate operations whose required grids are unavailable locally.
projinfo --grid-check=none ignores grid availability and can report operations as if required grids were available.
projinfo --grid-check=known_available accepts locally available grids or grids known to the CDN and is the network-enabled default strategy.
projinfo --searchpaths reports the directories used for PROJ resource lookup.
projinfo --remote-data reports whether PROJ network capability is enabled and the related remote URL.
projinfo --main-db-path can pin the exact proj.db used for coordinate-operation discovery.
projinfo supports one or more auxiliary PROJ databases, which can add definitions to the main database and must therefore be part of provenance.
cs2cs --only-best forces use of the best transformation known by PROJ and errors when a grid required by that best transformation is missing.
cs2cs --no-ballpark disallows coordinate operations containing ballpark transformations.
cs2cs --accuracy sets a minimum desired accuracy threshold for candidate coordinate operations.
PROJ pipelines are ordered sequences of coordinate-operation steps, so exact step order is semantic provenance.
cct can instantiate an explicit coordinate operation or operation identifier rather than asking PROJ to choose implicitly at execution time.
cct can use remote grids when PROJ_NETWORK=ON and required grids are not available locally.
PROJ grid database lookup can report a grid full filename, package name, URL, direct-download flag, open-license flag and runtime availability.
PROJ grid metadata exposes grid name, filename, format, extent, dimensions and cell spacing for runtime provenance.
PROJ coordinate-operation computation filters candidates by user-requested minimum accuracy.
PROJ coordinate-operation computation filters candidates by area of use.
PROJ coordinate-operation computation can filter candidates based on missing required grids.
CoordinateOperationContext can explicitly disallow ballpark transformations, making that policy inspectable rather than implicit.
The current official download page lists PROJ 9.8.1 as the current release dated 2026-04-10.
The current official download page lists proj-data 1.24 dated 2025-12-01, so code version and data-package version are distinct provenance fields.
OSTN15 and OSGM15 are the Ordnance Survey models linking GNSS-derived ETRS89 positions to British National Grid coordinates and mean-sea-level-based heights.
Grid InQuest II uses OSTN15/OSGM15 and can operate as installed desktop software without an online service.
OSTN15/OSGM15 replaced OSTN02/OSGM02 in August 2016.
Ordnance Survey publishes developer resources for incorporating OSTN15 transformation and OSGM15 geoid models into software.
